neighbours.label: The final piece of a split plural noun for recurring crises or periods (recess|ions, depress|ions, pand|emics, epid|emics, fam|ines, pl|agues, intergl|acial, glac|iations); the same kinds of event as single tokens (crises, wars, floods, outbreaks, recession, pandemic) stay quiet.
fire: Economists compared the two recessions in detail.
Farmers survived several depressions in the 1800s.
Doctors study how pandemics spread between cities.
Cholera epidemics struck the port every few years.
Repeated famines drove families to the coast.
Several glaciations shaped the valley floor.
Market slumps hurt small shops the most.
quiet: Economists compared the two crises in detail.
Farmers survived several wars in the 1800s.
Doctors study how a pandemic spreads between cities.
Cholera outbreaks struck the port every few years.
Repeated floods drove families to the coast.
Medieval invasions emptied whole villages, the chroniclers wrote.
Several rivers shaped the valley floor.
Market crashes hurt small shops the most.

predictions: fire 0.3-1.2; near misses below 0.2 (invasions may fire)
short: final piece of split crisis/period plurals
notes: Round 2 for this pole (round 1 in sweep 5: 'climate eras' failed; 'interglacial' fired 0.55-0.70 but 'global warming' and 'ice age' did not, and 'past epidemics' 0.30 fired as a near miss).
